Let’s dive into Chapter 2 — Understanding Influence and the Nature of Followership.
Now that you’ve got credibility on your side, what’s next? It’s all about figuring out how real influence works, and why people actually choose to follow someone.
Here’s the thing: leadership isn’t just about handing out orders. It’s about sparking that voluntary commitment in others. Influence isn’t something you get just because of your job title—it’s something you earn.
So, what’s the difference between authority and influence? Authority comes from your role or title, sure. But influence? That’s your real superpower. It’s the ability to shape how people think, act, and even how things turn out, without relying on official power. A leader with true influence can inspire action, even when they don’t have direct control. See, authority might force compliance, but only influence can spark real engagement and loyalty.
Why do people choose to follow? Well, it usually comes down to three big reasons:
First, trust. People need to believe their leader means well and can actually deliver. Second, shared values. When folks feel their own principles line up with a leader’s vision, they’re far more likely to get on board. And third, personal connection. Think about how motivating it is to feel seen, heard, and valued.
Picture this: there’s a team leader who always stands up for the team, communicates openly, and recognizes everyone’s unique contributions. Wouldn’t you be more likely to go above and beyond for that person? Not because you have to—but because you want to.
Let’s talk about what I like to call the Influence Equation: Influence equals Credibility, times Connection, times Shared Purpose.
If any piece of that equation is missing, your influence starts to falter. Maybe you’re a total expert, but you can’t relate to others. Or, maybe you’re warm and approachable, but you don’t deliver results. Either way, the equation just doesn’t add up.
Building connection is key. It’s about empathy, active listening, and genuinely caring about what matters to other people. Leaders who take time to understand what drives their colleagues—who ask questions and listen without judging—build a real sense of belonging. That’s the bridge influence travels across.
And then there’s shared purpose. When people know what they’re working toward, and they see how their efforts fit into the bigger picture, they care more. You don’t need grand speeches here. It’s about weaving purpose into everyday chats and decisions, making sure everyone’s part of the story.
Here’s something important: followership isn’t automatic. People don’t just fall in line because you’re the boss. You have to earn it—through trustworthy actions, meaningful connections, and by showing you’re all moving toward the same goals. When leaders focus on these things, folks will stick with them, even when times get tough.
So, how can you build your own influence in practical ways? Try this:
Spend real time learning what matters to others.
Share your vision in ways that make sense to people’s everyday lives.
Celebrate all kinds of contributions—big wins and small moments alike.
And above all, be fully present when you interact, showing that everyone truly matters.
Remember, influence doesn’t just stop with your direct reports. It ripples outward, touching peers, leaders above you, and even people outside your organization. When you build influence, you create networks—support, collaboration, and a bigger impact than you might imagine.
So, here’s the takeaway: influence is the real currency of leadership. It’s earned by building credibility, forging connections, and rallying around a shared purpose. That’s what transforms simple authority into genuine, inspiring leadership.
